chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sufi narrated to me from Yusuf ibn Aqil from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, who said:

When Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) arrived in Nishapur and intended to travel from there to al-Ma'mun, the narrators of traditions gathered around him and said to him: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, you are leaving us without narrating a tradition from which we may benefit.' He was seated in the camel saddle, so he put his head out and said:

'I heard my father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: I heard my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: I heard my father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying: I heard my father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying: I heard my father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: I heard my father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying: I heard my father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: I heard Jibril (Gabriel) saying: I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:
'La ilaha illallah (There is no god but Allah) is My fort, and whoever enters My fort will be safe from My punishment.'
When the camel moved, he loudly said: 'There are certain conditions for this [statement], and I am one of these conditions.'

key_terms.حَدِیثٌ قُدْسِی: Divine tradition (implied by chain to Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'La ilaha illallah' as a fort according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) delivers a Hadith Qudsi in Nishapur, tracing the divine declaration that 'La ilaha illallah' is Allah’s fortress and guarantee of safety from punishment back through the Imams to the Prophet and Gabriel. In a unique Shia scholarly nuance, he identifies himself as one of the 'conditions' (shurut) for this promise, implying that true entry into the fortress requires recognition of his Imamate alongside the declaration of monotheism. This highlights the Shia doctrine that the Imams are the living proof and necessary context for the validity of faith.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said it was narrated to me by Abu al-Hassan al-Asadi who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hussain al-Sufi from Yusif b. ’Aqeel from Ishaq b. Rahawayh who said:

When Imam Reza (a.s.) reached Nishapur and intended to go to Mamoon, the narrators of traditions gathered around him and said, “O son of Allah’s Messenger! You are leaving us without having said any tradition, which could benefit us.” Imam (a.s.) was seated in the camel saddle. He put his head out and said,

“I heard my father, Musa Ibne Ja’far (a.s.), who says he heard from his father, Ja’far Ibne Muhammad (a.s.), who says he heard from his father, Muhammad Ibne Ali (a.s.), who says he heard from his father, Ali Ibne Husain (a.s.), who says he heard from his father, Husain Ibne Ali (a.s.), who says he heard from his father, Amirul Momineen Ali Ibne Abi Talib (a.s.), who says he heard from the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.s.), who says he heard from Jibraeel, who says he heard from Almighty Allah that,
‘The statement Laa ilaaha illallaah is My fort. One who enters My fort will remain safe from My punishment.”
When they moved on, he loudly said: “There are certain conditions for this. And I am one of these conditions.”
